transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (Head of Data & ML - Starlight), Carlos Gomez (CTO - Starlight), Ellen Rivers (Clinical AI Lead - Starlight)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through the POC scope for the quality evaluation plan, try to keep it focused — hi Maya, hi Carlos, hi Ellen
00:06 Maya: hi Jordan, hi Priya, thanks for doing this. We're hoping to validate accuracy and reduce hallucinations on our discharge summary generator. 
00:12 Jordan: perfect, quick intros, Priya is our solutions engineer who will run benchmarks and outline the test harness.
00:17 Priya: hey all, brief note — we'll be using Redwood hosted dev environment, unless you need VPC/private from the start, which we can discuss.
00:24 Carlos: for now hosted is fine as long as it's de-identified and meets our security checks, we may move to private during pilot.
00:30 Jordan: great. So high-level agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark metrics, golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring approach, timeline and next steps. Sound good?
00:38 Ellen: yep

03:05 Priya: starting with success criteria — from our pre-call you listed top items: clinical accuracy (match to ground truth), hallucination rate below X, format fidelity (templated discharge format), end-to-end latency under Y for 95th percentile, and cost per 1k tokens within target. Can you confirm or add?
03:17 Maya: yes, clinical accuracy is primary, we also want hallucination measured separately (false facts vs omission), and output structure must align with our EHR ingestion format. Also want a subjective clinician score — i.e. clinicians rate summaries 1-5.
03:28 Priya: good, so suggested concrete thresholds: clinical accuracy >= 92% on gold set, hallucination rate < 3% on sampled outputs, formatting compliance >= 98%, clinician mean rating >= 4.0. Are these realistic?
03:40 Carlos: 92% sounds ambitious but okay for POC — it's fine as a target. We may adjust if initial baseline is lower.

06:05 Jordan: workload sizing — what's realistic for POC? We proposed 500 golden records with 2,000 additional random samples for regression and edge cases. Thoughts?
06:15 Maya: 500 de-identified gold records with clinician-annotated expected outputs is doable but will take a week to prepare. The additional 2k can be synthetic or sampled from historical de-identified.
06:25 Priya: perfect. For benchmarks we'll run deterministic generation with set temperature and top-p; we'll also run a small sweep across quantization/model variants to check tradeoffs. Baseline models we plan to test: redwood/ggml-like open model (we'll list specifics in doc), plus a higher-capacity variant.
06:40 Ellen: quick Q — how do you handle KV cache and long history? Our discharge summaries have long context (patient notes + labs).
06:48 Priya: we can simulate typical context lengths and measure latency and throughput. Redwood runtime handles continuous batching and KV cache; we'll test sequence lengths up to 8k tokens for the POC. Note: sometimes transcription will call it 'Redwood runtime' or 'runtime engine' which may be mis-transcribed in notes.

10:12 Jordan: benchmarks — primary metrics: clinical accuracy (token/phrase level F1?), hallucination count per document, formatting error rate, 95/99 P latency, cost per 1k tokens. Secondary: memory usage, throughput for batching.
10:25 Priya: for accuracy, we suggest a mixed scoring: automated metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore) for broad signal + exact-match checks for templated fields (e.g., medication list, doses) + clinician judgment on a sampled subset.
10:40 Maya: we care most about the templated fields being exact; free-text areas can use fuzzy metrics. Also we need hallucination taxonomy — i.e., invented medication vs wrong dosage vs invented dates.
10:52 Priya: we'll build hallucination checks as rule-based detectors plus sampling for clinician review. We'll report hallucination as counts and severity buckets.

14:00 Ellen: on regression tests — can you explain what that looks like?
14:05 Priya: sure. Regression suite will contain: golden prompts + golden outputs (the 500), transformation tests (e.g., reorder sections, redaction), format tests (EHR importability), and adversarial prompts to trigger hallucinations. Every model change or config change will be run through the suite and produce a delta report.
14:22 Jordan: important to tie regressions to alerts: if clinician score drops by 0.2, or hallucination increases >1% absolute, we flag.

17:30 Maya: golden prompts — are these hand-curated or auto-generated?
17:34 Priya: hand-curated by your clinical team for the gold set. We'll provide templates. Example golden prompt: "Given patient notes and labs, produce discharge summary with sections: Diagnosis, Hospital Course, Medications (name|dose|freq), Follow-up." We'll store prompt+expected output pairs in the shared spreadsheet.
17:50 Maya: good, we'll add typical edge cases — multi-morbidity, conflicting meds, nursing notes only.

20:10 Jordan: hallucination/format checks — practical approach: 1) automated entity extraction from model output and compare to input entities (meds, labs), 2) rule-based detectors for impossible values (e.g., negative doses), 3) clinician review sampling for false positives.
20:25 Carlos: how do you quantify hallucination severity?
20:30 Priya: severity buckets: critical (invented diagnosis/medication that could cause harm), major (wrong dosage), minor (format/typo). We'll count incidence per 100 outputs and weight by severity for an overall hallucination score.

23:50 Ellen: scoring approach — propose composite score with weights: clinical accuracy 50%, hallucination-adjusted score 25%, format compliance 15%, clinician subjective 10%. Thoughts?
24:05 Maya: that seems reasonable but maybe increase clinician subjective to 15% and reduce accuracy to 45% to reflect human-in-the-loop priorities.
24:15 Jordan: can do. We'll record weights in the eval plan and allow you to modify. The final POC pass criteria will be composite >= 85% (or configurable).

27:30 Priya: technical test harness — we'll produce a reproducible runbook: env config (model name, quantization, batch sizes), prompt templates, post-processing scripts (regex for meds), and scoring notebooks. We'll host run results in a shared Google Sheet and a CSV export for your systems.
27:50 Carlos: any data residency concerns for hosted runs? We need confirmation that de-identified data stays within the US region and logs are controlled.
27:58 Jordan: we'll include region spec and retention policies. For POC hosted, logs are ephemeral and we can disable transcript storage. If you need VPC/private we can spin that up but it adds ~2 weeks to timeline.

31:10 Maya: timeline check — what's a realistic POC timeline?
31:15 Priya: proposed: week 0 (this call) finalize eval plan and sample prep; week 1 send golden set + 2k samples; week 2 baseline runs and initial metrics; week 3 clinician review sample and regression adjustments; week 4 final report and go/no-go decision. So ~4 weeks.
31:30 Carlos: that fits our internal cadence, though compliance review may push to 5-6 weeks.

34:00 Jordan: risks and mitigations — primary risk is low baseline quality; mitigations: try larger model variant or tune prompts; cost risk — mitigate with quantization and batching. Also hallucination edge cases — we'll suggest guardrails like extractor-based verification before EHR ingestion.
34:18 Ellen: can you demo the hallucination detector? maybe later in a technical deep dive.
34:22 Priya: yes, we can schedule SE-led session to walk through rule-based checks and the detector pipeline.

36:50 Jordan: artifacts we'll share after call: eval plan doc (detailed), prompt templates, shared spreadsheet for golden prompts & outputs, runbook for benchmark, and SSO/KMS security doc.
36:58 Maya: please include an example CSV schema for the sample exports so our engineering can prep.
37:05 Jordan: will do.

40:45 Priya: one more technical note — when we compare models we'll also include a small ablation on quantization (8-bit/4-bit) to show cost vs quality tradeoff. Expect minor degradation but large cost savings in some cases.
40:58 Carlos: important to see the delta numbers, especially on hallucination.

44:10 Ellen: clinician scoring logistics — we'll provide 5 clinicians to rate 100 samples each over week 3, is that acceptable?
44:18 Priya: yes that should give statistically useful signals; we'll provide a simple UI/spreadsheet for scoring with guidance to reduce rater variance.

47:30 Jordan: recap and next steps? Maya, can you confirm who owns providing the de-identified samples and when?
47:36 Maya: I'll own the gold set, my team will de-id and annotate 500 records, target delivery 2026-10-06. Carlos will handle compliance signoff.
47:45 Carlos: yes I'll confirm compliance contact by 2026-10-05.
47:50 Jordan: perfect. We'll send the eval plan and prompts by 2026-10-02 and schedule the SE benchmark run for the week of 2026-10-12.

50:10 Priya: small note — sometimes Fireflies transcriptions auto-change product names, you'll see 'Red wood' or 'redwood runtime' in auto text; ignore those.
50:20 Maya: ha, noted.

51:00 Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the doc and calendar invites. Any last questions?
51:08 Ellen: none from me, thanks.
51:12 Carlos: all good.
51:20 Maya: thanks everyone.

51:30 Jordan: meeting ends.

References and artifacts shared: "Quality Eval Plan (draft)" link, shared spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/EXAMPLE-GOLDEN-PROMPTS, runbook.csv example attached in follow-up.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps and punctuation artifacts present; speaker labels approximate.
